core.title: An absent change set is COULD_NOT_CHECK (blocks), never 'nothing undeclared'
core.given: A plan's work has a recorded documentation declaration.
core.when: core supplies no change set at all, as opposed to an empty one.
core.then: The documentation check returns COULD_NOT_CHECK, which blocks. It never reports 'nothing undeclared'.
prefer: Read an empty change set as 'nothing changed' (permits), and an absent change set as COULD_NOT_CHECK (blocks).
avoid: Treating an absent change set as an empty one, or reporting 'nothing undeclared' when no change set was supplied.
unless: No declaration is recorded at all. That case belongs to core, not to this rule.
core.why: An ABSENT change set is not an empty one. Without a change set, the check is in no position to claim that nothing is undeclared. An empty change set is core saying that nothing changed, which is actionable. The two stay distinct for the same reason NOT_APPLICABLE and COULD_NOT_CHECK do (spec 2 §3).
evidence: With an absent change set, the result is COULD_NOT_CHECK and it blocks.
With an empty change set, the result permits.
The two results are never conflated.
verification: The change set is handed to the check by core; the check reads it and never computes it, so a missing change set cannot be filled in locally.
Absent: return COULD_NOT_CHECK, which blocks; never report 'nothing undeclared', because the check is in no position to make that claim. Empty: nothing changed, which is actionable and permits.
Keep absent and empty distinct for the same reason NOT_APPLICABLE and COULD_NOT_CHECK must stay distinct (spec 2 §3).
If no documentation declaration is recorded, this check does not fire; defer to core's declaration check (companion §4, check 1).
Severity 2, strict disposition: the check fails on every finding; no advisory mode, no ratchet baseline.

The observer must tell apart a change set that core did not supply at all (absent) from one that core supplied with no paths (empty); the rule fires on the absent case even when no changed paths are observable.

fires: A documentation declaration is recorded for the work, but core supplies no change set at all. The rule cannot be evaluated, so the check returns COULD_NOT_CHECK, which blocks.
doesNotFire: Core supplies an empty change set. That means nothing changed: the result is actionable and permits.
Core supplies a non-empty change set. The sibling rule that evaluates declaration coverage of the changed paths owns that case.
No documentation declaration is recorded at all. That is core's concern (companion §4, check 1).

neutralityNotes: This rule is a framework-semantics rule about classifying an absent versus an empty change set. bun.json contains no stack-specific paths, suffixes, idioms or tools, so the core needs no profile data and profileRequirements is empty (the validator id docs_capability is explicitly not a profile key). Realization details left with the Bun rewrite: the validator id and the shared:policy.strict-disposition reference (bunOnly), and the sibling part id cover-docs-paths, which the core refers to generically as the sibling rule that evaluates declaration coverage of the changed paths. Corpus citations (spec 2 §3, companion §4 check 1, companion §5) were retained because they reference the stack-neutral ATDD corpus, exactly as the canonical source does. Realizing the two needs_new_observer facts (recognizing a recorded documentation declaration, and distinguishing an absent from an empty change set) is observer work of each realization; bun.json itself carries no concrete value for either. The audit and additions metadata of bun.json are split bookkeeping and stay with the realization.
